Project.Vision: Evolve the pedestrian-safety app into a broader civic operating system for mobility, infrastructure, sanitation, and municipal planning.

CurrentState.WhatExistsNow: Safety-first routing, live danger zone overlays, real-time navigation, SOS alerts, incident reporting, operator moderation, H3-based safety zones, and a FastAPI + Flutter + PostGIS + Valhalla stack.
CurrentState.RelevantREADMEReferences: WalkSafe currently prioritizes safety over speed, includes incident reporting and SOS, uses H3 zones, and already lists media uploads as a planned feature.

Module.name: SafeMobility
Module.Description: Safety-first pedestrian routing, SOS, danger-zone overlays, and incident-aware route updates.

Module.name: WasteManagement
Module.Description: Citizen reports for illegal dumping, overflowing bins, garbage burning, dead animals, and construction debris.

Module.name: InfrastructureReporting
Module.Description: Citizen reports for potholes, broken streetlights, damaged footpaths, fallen trees, broken signals, water leaks, and waterlogging.

Module.name: CivicAnalytics
Module.Description: Ward-level dashboards, heatmaps, trends, response metrics, and planning insights for authorities.

Module.name: DemoSeeder
Module.Description: Mock users, mock reports, sample images, seeded city layers, and instant demo dashboards.

Module.name: DeploymentProfiles
Module.Description: Local, demo, AWS, and production profiles that switch storage, tunnel, database, and hosting behavior by config.

Group.name: CitizenReporting
Group.Item: Photo + location + category + severity submission flow.
User-selected report labels instead of mandatory AI image classification.
Optional explanation/notes field.
Immediate dashboard visibility for authorities.

Group.name: MapAndScoring
Group.Item: H3-based aggregation and heatmap redraws.
Safety routing refresh every 6 hours.
Infrastructure and sanitation redraw every 36 to 48 hours.
Hourly ingestion of new reports.
Decay/aging of old reports so stale issues lose weight over time.

Group.name: Analytics
Group.Item: Ward-wise issue counts and hot spots.
Priority ranking of unresolved issues.
Weekly citywide summaries.
Natural-language summaries based on location + description only, if AI is used at all.

Group.name: DemoMode
Group.Item: Mock data seeding on competition day.
Prebuilt dashboards that look populated immediately.
Config-driven city switching without code changes.

Group.name: ProductDirection
Group.Item: Shift the project pitch from only pedestrian safety to broader city operations.
Keep WalkSafe as one module instead of the whole product.
Make the system useful even without always-on hosting or live users.

Group.name: DataAndBackend
Group.Item: Add category-based reporting for waste and infrastructure.
Store images in object storage in cloud mode, or local disk in local mode.
Replace any always-on AI image pipeline with user labeling and optional lightweight summarization.
Move heavy recomputation into scheduled jobs.
Separate live reports from derived heatmaps and analytics.

Group.name: Deployment
Group.Item: Support local-only runs for hackathons.
Support demo mode with seeded mock data.
Support AWS mode with containerized services.
Abstract storage, tunnels, and hosting behind config profiles.
Allow ngrok-based local public demos when needed.

Group.name: UIUX
Group.Item: Add category and severity forms.
Show images, labels, explanations, and map locations on the dashboard.
Make the app feel instant by deferring slow work to background jobs.

Profile.name: local
Profile.Item: Run everything on a laptop for development or competition day.
Use local storage or mounted disk for images.
Use ngrok or equivalent tunnel when a public URL is needed.
Use seeded mock data and short refresh intervals.

Profile.name: demo
Profile.Item: Run a polished competition demo with seeded data and precomputed layers.
Keep the stack containerized and repeatable.
Use mock users, reports, and images.
Expose the app publicly only for the duration of the demo.

Profile.name: aws
Profile.Item: Use ECS or a single EC2 + Docker Compose stack for a cheap pilot.
Use S3 for images and Supabase/Postgres for structured data.
Keep the same containers and switch behavior through config.

Profile.name: production
Profile.Item: CloudFront, managed storage, monitoring, and scheduled workers.
More frequent backups and stricter ops controls.

Stack.ObjectStorage: S3 in cloud mode; local storage in local mode

Notes.Principle: Optimize for reproducibility and low operating cost rather than perpetual hosting.
Notes.HackathonGoal: A judge should be able to run a fully populated demo from config and seed data on competition day.
